detail:
The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) lists the adult studies conducted by its intramural research program at the NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, Maryland. The depression studies described on the page include brain imaging studies in which researchers study the brains of people who are depressed, and depression evaluations that screen participants for medication and brain imaging studies, including studies of experimental medications researchers are examining for severe and hard-to-treat depressive symptoms.

Other studies on the page test investigational approaches under research conditions, including an investigational drug study and studies examining how specific brain receptors relate to antidepressant response, using brain imaging and neuroimaging alongside clinical evaluation. NIMH describes the studies as inpatient or outpatient research conducted by its own clinicians and scientists, separate from standard clinical care, with eligibility assessed by the study teams.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about depression research and clinical trials.
summary: NIMH lists its intramural adult depression studies at the NIH Clinical Center, including brain imaging studies, evaluations that screen for medication and imaging studies, and trials of investigational approaches for hard-to-treat symptoms.
takeaways: nimh intramural studies are conducted at the nih clinical center in bethesda
studies described include brain imaging and investigational medication research
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Depression: where depression research is heading
